_note: The agentic loop's own limits (local-ai-engine.md §4.6). THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) the loop is depth-capped at 32, mirroring the action grammar — a model that keeps calling tools forever is stopped by the runtime with a typed error, not by the battery. (2) A tool may not call the model that is running it: a tool invocation resolving to the `intelligence` scheme (or the loop's own model) is refused TYPED rather than self-deadlocking under single-flight — governor-scheduled nesting is a later relaxation, never a v1 accident. (3) Cancelling mid-loop stops the whole loop, not just the current engine turn: no tool dispatched after the cancel. (4) The loop keeps a local ring-buffered transcript — prompts, decisions, tool calls, approvals — exportable from the DevSettings drawer and NEVER transmitted; it is what makes agentic behaviour debuggable on the pillars' terms. (5) An unknown tool name coming back from the model is answered typed and fed to the model, which is how a hallucinated tool becomes a correction instead of a crash.

cases.name: loop: the depth cap stops a runaway tool loop typed
cases._note: The mock calls the same tool on every turn forever. The runtime stops at depth 32 with `tool_depth_exceeded` and settles the request — the count is asserted exactly so an off-by-one does not silently double the work.

cases.name: loop: a tool may not call the model that is running it
cases._note: The no-self-call law. A tool row pointing back at the `intelligence` scheme is refused with a typed error that rides back to the model as the tool result; nothing dispatches and the loop does not deadlock waiting on its own engine.

cases.name: loop: an unknown tool name answers typed and the model corrects
cases._note: Models invent tool names. The runtime answers `tool_unknown` as the tool result instead of failing the request, and the next turn is the model's correction.

cases.name: loop: cancelling mid-loop dispatches nothing further
cases._note: Cancellation is loop-wide. After the cancel the runtime does not start the next turn and does not dispatch the tool the model asked for on the turn that was already in flight.

cases.name: loop: the transcript records the run and stays on the device
cases._note: The audit trail the pillars require. Every prompt, tool call, approval decision and completion lands in a local ring buffer that a developer can export from DevSettings; `transmitted` is asserted false because a transcript that phones home would be the backdoor the whole program denies having.
